overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford City Council candidate Patrick Clerkin to discuss his platform, which focuses on zoning, charter reform, commercial growth, municipal overrides, and street repairs.

items.title: Show Introduction and Candidate Invitation
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced the program and invited Medford City Council and School Committee candidates to appear on the show.

items.title: Zoning and Affordable Housing
items.summary: Candidate Patrick Clerkin discussed building community support for affordable housing zoning through clear maps, forming a community advisory council, and pursuing public and private funding partnerships.

items.title: Proposed City Charter Revision
items.summary: Clerkin expressed support for the proposed city charter revision, highlighting benefits like ward-based representation, a ten-year review cycle, and an accelerated budget timeline.

items.title: Commercial Revenue and Expense Management
items.summary: Clerkin proposed simplifying the commercial permitting process, establishing business incentive packages, and renegotiating town-and-gown relations with Tufts University and the Chevalier Theatre to increase revenue.

items.title: Municipal Overrides for Fire Station and High School
items.summary: Clerkin supported the underlying fire station project and favored strategic renovation over a brand-new high school build, but expressed skepticism toward municipal tax overrides as "financial duct tape."

items.title: Street Infrastructure, Arts, and Veterans Services
items.summary: Clerkin discussed sharing the city's street repair priority map, consolidating decentralised arts groups, and potentially housing the veterans affairs office at the American Legion.

items.title: Campaign Contact and Show Closing
items.summary: Clerkin shared his website, upcoming fundraiser details, and campaign contact information before Petrella concluded the broadcast.
